entries.description: In this talk by Uber Eats, we learn from the biggest payment processor that “growing businesses with declining loss rates is extremely rare in the industry”. Also, fraud can takes several forms: chargebacks on non-perishable goods, promo abuse, refunds…

entries.name: KYC and AML: beyond the acronyms
entries.description: KYC is nuanced and fuzzy, because it is a stochastic process to reduce risk.

entries.name: Awesome Fraud Detection Research Papers
entries.description: Papers sourced from several conferences on all sort of fraud: credit card, payment transactions, loans, customs inspections, money laundering networks, and more.

entries.name: Tazama
entries.description: 🆓 Open-source real-time transaction monitoring software for fraud and money laundering detection, governed by the Tazama Linux Foundation project. This is just an engine to define rules, weight them, and apply them to transactions. There is nothing specific to payments or financial transactions.

entries.name: Mojaloop Fraud Risk Management
entries.description: 🆓 Concrete AML rule implementations from the Mojaloop Foundation: transaction mirroring (90-100% amount-match window), multi-tier payee-graph traversal for layering detection, account-dormancy reactivation, large-transaction-payer, new-payee-transfer. Repo is archived but the rules are static reference material rarely seen elsewhere in OSS.

entries.name: Reproducible Machine Learning for Credit Card Fraud detection
entries.description: A practical handbook on how to identify patterns in transactions.

entries.name: How I Stopped a Credit Card Thief From Ripping Off 3,537 People – and Saved Our Nonprofit in the Process
entries.description: Describe a fraud technique known as "card testing", in which massive batch of stolen cards are checked for their validity against your API.

entries.name: How Candy Japan got credit card fraud somewhat under control
entries.description: Suggestions involved either warning signals for trying to guess which orders might be fraud, or countermeasures to try to make things harder for the fraudsters.

entries.name: Five Fun Fraud Facts
entries.description: Another tiny collection of features we can feed to a ML system to detect fraud. Comments on HN also unearthed more qualifying signals and derived geodata on the transaction.

entries.name: Credit Card Fraud Detection using Autoencoders in Keras
entries.description: Tutorial on how to rely on anomaly detection to implement suspicious card transactions.

entries.name: Training an ML model to score chargebacks
entries.description: An example of a platform's network effect, which allows to predict the likelihood of winning a dispute.

entries.name: How credit card thieves use free-to-play apps to launder gains
entries.description: To prevent abuses, service provider must strengthen both credit card verification and the account creation process.

entries.name: GCP improved account management policies to better support customers
entries.description: Or why relying too much on fraud automation might lead to disgruntled users.

entries.name: Digital Ocean's Update on Customer Shutdown Incident
entries.description: Aggressively shutting down user servers is good from a business point of view to prevent fraudster abusing free resources, until it's not.

entries.name: Awesome Credit Modeling
entries.description: How to use statistical methods to classify applicants into categories to reduce risks. Lots of inspiration and research papers there to improve general scoring.

entries.name: Benford's law
entries.description: Digit distribution can be a signal of accounting fraud.

entries.name: Integer percentages as electoral falsification fingerprints
entries.description: In the same spirit as above, this paper show that frequency of reported round numbers in election is a signal of man-made anomalies. Might be applicable in some fraud-fighting area.

entries.name: Huber loss
entries.description: “A loss function used in robust regression, that is less sensitive to outliers in data than the squared error loss.”

entries.name: Peak Detection in the Python World
entries.description: Simple way to detect outliers.

entries.name: Method to check if you swapped 2 digits
entries.description: Standard manual accounting trick employed when isolating an error in a double ledger.

entries.name: More than 600 million users installed Android 'fleeceware' apps from the Play Store
entries.description: A new kind of fraud, in which apps silently keep charging users after the end of the trial period.

entries.name: CEO Fraud
entries.description: A billing team responsible for collecting payment is prey to this kind of fraud, in which the CEO is impersonated to commend exceptional payment transactions.

entries.name: The Challenges of Operating a Computing Cloud and Charging for its Use
entries.description: Skip the first 90% of this presentation by an AWS VP (which is about general system reliability). The last four slides are a good summary of what billing cloud services entails, especially the use of soft quotas to limit fraud.

entries.name: Fraud in Telephony Networks
entries.description: Most of telephony frauds gravitates around billing and the metering of micro-transactions. This paper feature a taxonomy (on page 6) differentiating the root causes, vulnerabilities, exploitation techniques, and the way fraudsters can benefits from them.

entries.name: Apple In-app purchase Human Interface Guidelines
entries.description: Guide and recommendation on how to make auto-renewable subscriptions user-friendly.

entries.name: Which has a higher conversion rate: A single long ecommerce checkout form or a multi-step one?
entries.description: Focus first on other things in the cart, like easing anxiety and second-guessing by adding reassurance (trust marks, testimonials) near the credit card and completion steps, as well as some guarantee language that you may have used earlier in the product exploration process.

entries.name: We tried to make billing backendless
entries.description: Failed attempt to move the billing experience by from backend to frontend because of security.

entries.name: Pricing pages design
entries.description: A collection of pricing pages from various SaaS companies, to get inspiration on how to present your offers.

entries.name: Startup financial models - 12 templates compared for SaaS
entries.description: A great source of inspiration to get better visibility in your operations.

entries.name: 16 Startup Metrics
entries.description: The 2 critical metrics being Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) and Customer Lifetime Value (CLV).

entries.name: Thinking about growth and profit
entries.description: Discuss the relationship between investments, profit and growth, and how it influence decisions on pricing, free trials and plan structure.

entries.name: A Quantitative Approach to Product Market Fit
entries.description: Metrics produced above have a greater reach, as they're used as important signals to validate product-market fit.

entries.name: Startup growth calculator
entries.description: Simple yet effective interactive profitability calculator for startups.

entries.name: An Overview of Visa
entries.description: Great breakdown of Visa business models and metrics.

entries.name: The SaaS Financial Model You'll Actually Use
entries.description: A complete tour of the financials of a startup, which gives you extra-context on how the metrics you produce fit into the larger picture.

entries.name: You're all calculating churn rates wrong
entries.description: “On the surface, churn rate may seem like a natural proxy for changes in customer lifetimes. Let's dig into why that is not true.” Churn rate is not a meaningful metric to compute CLV: during the customer lifetime, the churn probability is not constant. Most of the time because of your free trial and vouchers. This article illustrate the influence of the distribution used to model the probability of a customer quitting.

entries.name: How to project customer retention
entries.description: A seminal paper, with a stronger approach compared to the one above: the exponential distributions is replaced by a geometric model, which is better suited to discrete time intervals like monthly contracts, the former being more appropriate to continuous time process.

entries.name: Survival Analysis For Customer Retention
entries.description: Illustrates how retention can be better modelled using a survival function like Kaplan–Meier survival curves.

entries.name: RFM (customer value)
entries.description: A refined model of CLV, used to segment users based on Recency, Frequency and Monetary value.

entries.name: Churn Prediction
entries.description: “How to use Python in a simplistic way to fuel your company's growth by applying the predictive approach to all your actions.” Relies on XGBoost binary classification.

entries.name: PyMC-Marketing
entries.description: 🆓 A full-featured Python package to analyze your users based on their "alive" and "dead" states. Apache-2.0 library stewarded by PyMC Labs, which only sells consulting services around it (no paid library tier).

entries.name: AI vs Data Science vs Data Engineering
entries.description: “Data Engineers build data pipelines and infrastructure to ensure a constant availability of transformed data. Data Scientists analyze and build models from these data to develop new product features or drive the bottom line of the business.” As for AI professionals, their focus is on cognitive automation.

entries.name: Ten Ways Your Data Project is Going to Fail
entries.description: You don't need data scientists. “For ETL, hire data engineers. For reporting, hire BI analysts. The end.”

entries.name: Cargo cult data science
entries.description: “Data science is best viewed as a form of company culture, rather than a set of technologies. However, many firms will try to create that company culture by acquiring data-science technology, rather than working on their culture.”

entries.name: Why not use Double or Float to represent currency?
entries.description: Because of precision: floats and doubles cannot accurately represent the base 10 multiples that we use for money.

entries.name: Never Use Floats for Money
entries.description: “This is precisely the problem we have when trying to represent 10^-1, or 0.1 in binary. There is not an exact binary representation of 0.1 or 0.01.”

entries.name: The Soul of an Old Machine: Revisiting the Timeless von Neumann Architecture
entries.description: Floats were suspicious even before the first general-purpose computer (EDVAC) was built: “Von Neumann wasn't entirely sold on why we might need floating-point numbers. He was quite vocal in his critique of floating-point numbers.” The author of this article complement this critique by illustrating the issue of precision and rounding.

entries.name: European Spreadsheet Risks Interest Group - Horror Stories
entries.description: A collection of cases in which uncontrolled and untested spreadsheet models led to lost revenue, mispricing, poor decision making, fraud and systemic financial failure.

entries.name: Practical Business Python
entries.description: A blog collecting and spreading ideas on how to use Python more effectively in the business setting.

entries.name: redash
entries.description: 🆓 Connect and query your data sources, build dashboards to visualize data and share them with your company. Owned by Databricks but the hosted SaaS shut down in 2021, so the project is now community-maintained under the Databricks org with no paid Redash product.

entries.name: Apache Superset
entries.description: 🆓 Enterprise-ready business intelligence web application, governed by the Apache Software Foundation.

entries.name: Meltano
entries.description: 🆓 Open source convention-over-configuration product for the whole data lifecycle, all the way from loading data to analyzing it. Meltano only sells managed Cloud hosting and support SLA on top of the OSS core.

entries.name: Patents on billing systems of the dot-com era
entries.description: All of them have been abandoned and constitute prior art. This means there is nothing to prevent anybody to implement or commercialize these concepts.

entries.description: A wrap-up of recent GCP pricing features.

entries.description: GCP's billing subsidiary.

entries.name: DigitalOcean Billing changelog
entries.description: All the latest billing updates on DO.

entries.name: Product Development as Iterated Taste
entries.description: AWS sacrificed the simplicity of subscription pricing for S3 and went instead with a safe cost-following strategy because they had no clue how the users will use their service.

entries.name: Israel demanded Google and Amazon use secret 'wink' to sidestep legal orders
entries.description: Invoicing of random fees with coded amounts were used as a hidden signal to bypass legal obligations. Maybe that's why you need a flexible billing system after all.

entries.name: £sd computing
entries.description: The IBM 1401 mainframe (1959) optionally supported pounds/shillings/pence (£sd) currency arithmetics in hardware.

entries.name: Engineering and Operations in the Bell System
entries.description: Starting at page #445, the "10.5 Billing Equipment and Systems" section describe the history and technical evolutions of Bell's phone calls metering and pricing.

entries.name: The vanished grandeur of accounting
entries.description: Accounting paintings were a significant genre in Dutch art.

entries.name: Graphic methods for presenting facts
entries.description: A way to optimize pricing using a physical model made in plaster of Paris, from 1914.
